description:
## Goal

Eliminate repeated root-granular transport derivation caused by subscribing aggregate products to intermediate settlement waves. Root products may join exact per-member answers for final packaging, but they must not rebuild a root inventory whenever any member advances.

## Current signal at a3a9761d1

On one debug-interp request for `00420_enum_take_drop_split`:

- OutgoingEdgeFrontier: 42 settlements and 41 displacements.
- IncomingInputRelations: 42 settlements and 41 displacements.
- IncomingInputSlot: 283 settlements and 172 displacements.
- ExecutableFacts now shows only 2 displacements; CallableConstruction shows 2.

A displacement is abandoned derivation: an input moves before the product can publish, so its work is discarded and repeated. The two root-scoped relation products still reproduce on nearly every relevant settlement wave.

RuntimeDemand cone publication currently releases many member movements as a batch mechanism, so this ticket follows the reactive RuntimeDemand conversion. Re-measure first: if fz-kdt.4 removes the churn, close this ticket with the causal proof rather than adding another abstraction.

## Output contract

- Outgoing edge and incoming relation state is maintained at the smallest identity that owns the edge or slot.
- One edge movement invalidates only the exact local relation cells and final root readers that consumed it.
- RootBackendProduct assembles the current reachable answer from exact dependencies; it does not subscribe to or rebuild an intermediate whole-root inventory per wave.
- IncomingInputSlot production begins only when its authoritative inputs can settle; it does not race the ascent that creates those inputs.
- Equal local answers preserve generations and produce no displacement.
- Persistent root sessions retain unaffected relation products across requests.

## Strategy

1. Re-run the causal report after fz-kdt.4 and classify every remaining displacement by its moved fact or product.
2. Identify the earliest aggregate dependency that turns one local movement into root-wide invalidation.
3. Move ownership down to immutable edge, executable, or slot facts/products already named by the model.
4. Keep the final root join packaging-only and demand-driven.
5. Delete the old root-granular intermediate authority and its invalidation path.

Do not cache a root scan, add a second frontier registry, or split a product without an exact owner and consumer.

## TDD and acceptance

- A one-edge addition, removal, and equal reproduction each have exact evaluation and displacement counts.
- Redefining one reached leaf reevaluates only relations in its transitive product-reader closure.
- Redefining an unreachable function performs zero transport-relation work for the root.
- Frontier and relation displacements are zero unless a test names the exact unavoidable race.
- Root-level packaging runs only when its final reachable answer changes.
- Canonical programs and all three execution doors remain identical.

## Checks and documentation

Run focused product dependency tests, persistent-root edit tests, causal reports on all target fixtures, full library, single-threaded matrix, interp/run/build parity, and clippy with warnings denied. Update fact-engine, pipeline, transport documentation, performance instrumentation, and northstar; remove any superseded aggregate product and telemetry.
title: Make root-scoped transport relations react to edge changes, not settlement waves
